# Bracketsight

> Five decision engines for US money rules that turn on a threshold: federal
> student loan repayment, the 2026 OBBBA paycheck deductions, ACA premium tax
> credits, residential property tax assessment appeals, and residential trade
> contracts. Every rate, bracket, threshold and term is held in versioned JSON
> rule files with primary-source citations and a last-verified date, and is
> read from those files at build time rather than written into prose.

## How the site computes

- All arithmetic is deterministic and runs client-side. No language model
  computes, estimates, adjusts or checks any number anywhere on this site.
- Money is integer cents; rates are integer basis points. No floating-point
  currency.
- Rules live in dated, cited JSON. A figure shown to a reader carries the rule
  set version it came from and the date its citation was last read.
- There are no accounts, no database and no server-side storage. State lives in
  the browser (`localStorage`) and in the URL. Nothing a visitor enters is
  transmitted or retained.
- Open verification items are published rather than hidden. `KNOWN-GAPS.md` in
  the repository records 55 unresolved items across the five engines, and a
  figure resting on one discloses it at the point of use.

## Sections

- [/loans](/loans): Simulates all nine federal repayment plans month by month
  for up to 30 years and ranks them by total lifetime cost, including tax on a
  forgiven balance. Covers RAP, Tiered Standard, old and new IBR, PAYE, ICR,
  Standard, Graduated and Extended. Models the RAP interest waiver and $50
  principal match, the absence of a RAP payment cap, the PAYE and ICR sunset on
  1 July 2028, Parent PLUS consolidation eligibility, and the forfeiture of
  prior IBR/PAYE/ICR payment credit on switching to RAP. Rules from 34 C.F.R.
  §§ 685.208–685.209 as revised by the RISE final rule, 91 Fed. Reg. 23768.
- [/paycheck](/paycheck): Computes the four deductions added by P.L. 119-21 —
  qualified tips (IRC § 224), qualified overtime compensation (IRC § 225), the
  additional deduction for filers 65 and over, and qualified passenger vehicle
  loan interest — with their caps, occupation eligibility tests and MAGI
  phase-outs. Includes a W-2 checker for whether an employer reported the
  amounts the deductions depend on.
- [/aca](/aca): Computes the premium tax credit from household MAGI, family
  size and county, measures the exact distance in dollars to the 400% federal
  poverty line eligibility ceiling, prices what one additional dollar of income
  costs at that point, models cost-sharing reduction bands and the repayment of
  excess advance credit, and lists the MAGI reductions that move a household
  back under a threshold.
- [/property](/property): Assesses whether a residential property tax
  assessment is worth appealing, using comparable sales, the county's
  assessment level and its statutory relief model. Covers Cook County, Illinois
  and Bergen County, New Jersey, including New Jersey's Chapter 123 common
  level range. Returns "cannot determine" rather than an estimate where a
  required input, such as a municipal Director's Ratio, has not been sourced.
- [/trades](/trades): Produces a line-item estimate, an invoice and a
  residential contract for decks, interior painting and bathroom remodels, and
  states which clauses and prescribed notices a contract must carry in
  California, Texas, Florida, New York and Pennsylvania. The pricing dataset is
  placeholder reference data, not surveyed market pricing, and is labelled as
  such throughout; the contract-law requirements are cited to statute.

## Reference

- [/guides](/guides): Articles, grouped by tool. Every figure in a guide is
  read from the same rule file the corresponding tool runs on, so a guide and
  its tool cannot state different numbers.
- [/glossary](/glossary): Definitions of the terms these rules are written in —
  MAGI, FPL, discretionary income, applicable percentage, common level range,
  mechanic's lien and others — each with what it decides and a primary source.
  Individual anchors, e.g. `/glossary#common-level-range`.
- Each section carries its own methodology, sources, editorial policy,
  changelog and about pages, e.g. [/loans/methodology](/loans/methodology) and
  [/loans/sources](/loans/sources). The sources pages list every citation
  behind that engine with the date each was last verified.

## Limits

- Estimates under stated rules, not advice. Not a servicer, employer, insurer,
  county assessor or law firm.
- Figures are current as of the rule set version shown beside them. Several
  rule families expire annually — the HHS poverty guidelines each January, the
  IRS § 36B indexing revenue procedure each summer, New Jersey Director's
  Ratios each April.
- Where a figure rests on an assumption rather than a rule — the flat marginal
  tax rate applied to a forgiven balance, for example — it is labelled an
  assumption at the point it is shown.
- Contact for corrections: info@bracketsight.com
